name: What is the difference between a sliding glass door and a French door?
description: Sliding glass doors slide horizontally, saving space, while French doors swing open and offer a traditional look.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a sliding glass door and a French door?

acceptedAnswer.text: A sliding glass door operates by having one or more panels slide horizontally along a track, typically offering an unobstructed view and saving space. French doors, on the other hand, consist of one or two hinged panels that swing open, providing a more traditional aesthetic. When deciding, a practical tradeoff involves space utilization: sliding doors are ideal for smaller areas where swing space is limited, while French doors require clear floor space for their full opening arc.
